channel.title: Why Building Alone Is Dangerous | LINKUP Founder Journal
channel.description: Five in depth founder reports explaining why building a startup alone leads to burnout, blind spots, zero distribution, investor rejection, and lost market velocity.

item.title: Why Solo Founder Burnout Destroys Promising Startups Before Product Market Fit
item.description: Discover why building a startup alone triggers severe decision fatigue and emotional burnout before product market fit, and how a cofounder protects survival.

item.title: Why Building Alone Starves Your Startup Of Distribution And Revenue
item.description: Learn why solo founders fall into the build trap with zero customers, and why splitting engineering and distribution between two cofounders unlocks revenue.

item.title: The Echo Chamber Trap Why Solo Builders Ship Products Nobody Wants
item.description: Without an equal cofounder challenging bad assumptions, solo builders fall prey to confirmation bias and waste months engineering features nobody buys.

item.title: Why Venture Investors Quietly Reject Solo Founders As A Single Point Of Failure
item.description: Understand why accelerators and seed VCs view solo founders as a single point of failure, and why recruiting a strong cofounder unlocks investor conviction.

item.title: Why A Two Founder Team Ships Twice As Fast And Wins Every Competitive Market
item.description: See how context switching slows solo builders down while parallel execution lets two cofounders ship faster, learn faster, and win competitive markets.
